sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between the two opinions on the Divine Presence in the Temple as rooted in the concept of enclothing, where the Rambam sees it as a descent and limitation while the Ramban sees it as revealing the Unlimited, and both aspects were present.

translations.translation: And the explanation of the connection of the two opinions regarding the manner of the indwelling of the Shechinah in the Beis HaMikdash to the explanation that specifically the Name Havayah is the true attribute,
one can say,
that the point of difference between the two opinions is — the matter of enclothing.
For enclothing
(in general)
is a descent,
for that which is enclothed becomes contracted and changed according to the manner of the garment
(as above in section 8).
Therefore,
the opinion of the Rambam is that the indwelling of the Shechinah in the Beis HaMikdash was through a conduit,
because it is not applicable to say of Elokus that it contracted and changed to be in the category of a physical place.
And the opinion of the Ramban
(and so is the ruling of Chassidus)
[is] that this that the indwelling of the Shechinah in the Beis HaMikdash was in a manner of enclothing is not a descent, but on the contrary,
by means of the light being drawn down and enclothed in a physical place,
through this it is revealed that the light is unlimited
(as above in section 8).
And one can say,
that this that the Maamar brings also the opinion of the Rambam
[and adds that so is the opinion of the Rasa"g,
the Radak,
and others],
is,
because in the enclothing that was in the Beis HaMikdash there were both aspects.
For in the externality,
the enclothing
(even the enclothing of the Beis HaMikdash)
is a descent and contraction
— the foundation of the method of the Rambam.
And in the innerness,
the enclothing in the Beis HaMikdash is a revelation of the true Unlimited, that it is within His power to enclothe even in a physical place — the foundation of the method of the Ramban.
And to note,
that this matter
(that enclothing is a revelation of the true Unlimited)
was explained specifically in Chassidus,
because the inner dimension of Torah reveals the innerness that is in every matter.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of enclothing in the Temple parallel the enclothing of miracles in nature, and that the Avot's drawing down of the Name Sha-dai was a preparation for and contained the revelation of the Name Havayah at Matan Torah.

translations.translation: And based on this one can say,

that from the reasons that the Maamar brings for the two opinions regarding the manner of the indwelling of the Shechinah in the Beis HaMikdash, it is a hint that in this manner it is also regarding the enclothing of miracles in nature,
that there are in this two aspects.
The aspect in externality is,
that the root of the miracles that are clothed in nature is from a light that relates to the worlds,
that from the perspective of this revelation,
it is impossible for there to be a change and nullification of nature.
And the aspect in innerness is,
that through the enclothing of miracles in nature the true Unlimited is revealed,
that this that Ein Sof the Unlimited
(Who is above enclothing)
rules and dominates over nature is in a manner that even nature itself becomes according to His will.
But this matter is revealed specifically through miracles that are above nature.
For after one sees miracles that are above nature it is understood that the enclothing of miracles in nature is
(not because they do not have the power to overturn nature,
but rather)
in order to reveal that the dominion of Ein Sof over nature is also over nature itself.
And based on this one can say that this that the Avot drew down the revelation of the Name Sha-dai — "that I said 'enough' of My Elokus to every creature,"
a new revelation that was not before even in concealment
(as above in section 2 and section 5),
was a preparation for the revelation of the Name Havayah that was revealed at Matan Torah.
And moreover,
that this drawing down itself
(the drawing down of the revelation of E-l Sha-dai that the Avot drew down)
is the drawing down of the revelation of the Name Havayah,
because in innerness, even the miracles that are clothed in nature, the root of their drawing down is from Ein Sof Who is above relation to the worlds,
Havayah.
But the drawing down of the Name Havayah then was clothed in the Name E-l Sha-dai,
and at Matan Torah,
when the revelation of the Name Havayah was drawn down,
it was then revealed that this is also the innerness of the revelation of E-l Sha-dai that was drawn down by the Avot
(and in the manner explained above that after one sees miracles that are above nature it is revealed that this is also the innerness of the miracles that are clothed in nature).
And this is "And I appeared to the Avot as E-l Sha-dai, and My Name Havayah I did not make known to them" — "I was not recognized by them in My true attribute,"
that even to the Avot the revelation of the Name Havayah was drawn,
but then it was in concealment,
"I did not make known" — "I was not recognized."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Name Sha-dai in creation ("enough") is also for the purpose of revealing the Unlimited within the limited, and that all Names are true in that their purpose is the revelation of the truth of Havayah.

translations.translation: And 4)
And in greater depth one can say,
that in this manner it is also regarding the Name Sha-dai in the creation of the world — "that I said to My world 'enough'."
For since the intention and purpose of the measurement and limitation of the world
("that I said to My world 'enough'")
is that through the service of Torah and Mitzvos the revelation of the Unlimited will be drawn into the limited
(the Name Sha-dai — "that I said 'enough' of My Elokus to every creature,"
and through this the Unlimited of the Name Havayah),
therefore,
the matter of "that I said to My world 'enough'" in its innerness is that there will be in the limited a revelation of the Unlimited.
And one can say,
that this is that all the Names are true,
for their purpose of all the Names
(even of the Name Sha-dai — "that I said to My world 'enough',"
and even of the Name Elokim, whose gematria is nature)
is that there will be the revelation of the truth of Havayah.
But the connection of the Name Sha-dai in the creation of the world to the revelation of Havayah is,
that the intention in this "that I said to My world 'enough'" is in order that there will be in it a revelation of the Unlimited,
but in actuality,
the matter of "that I said to My world 'enough'" is to limit,
to conceal the Unlimited.
And the connection of the Name Sha-dai that was revealed to the Avot to the revelation of the Name Havayah is that then the revelation of the Unlimited of Havayah began in actuality,
and only that then
(still)
"I was not recognized in My true attribute."
